Scoring Machine: Scoring machines are pure bucket-getters, offensive weapons - they are unmatched in their ability to put the ball in the basket. With the ability to score from anywhere on the court, they are a nightmare to defend against. However, these players are also less likely to do anything else as well as they score, and need the ball in their hands.
Shot Creators: Shot creators are adept at making tough, contested shots and shots off the dribble. When the shot clock is winding down, just give the ball to these players and get out of the way. Because of this ability, however, shot creators are more likely to take 'bad' shots and will look worse when these shots are not falling.
All-Around: These players have no weakness - they are the Swiss Army knives of basketball. They can get it done on both ends of the floor and are most likely to be the glue a team needs to hold everything together. However, these players do not excel in a single area and so are less likely to be noticed.
Offensive Threat: These players high-level scorers, able to get it done from anywhere on the court on the offensive end. When you need a bucket, these are your go-to players. Offensive threats are offence-focused, meaning their defence and overall game are often lacking; this means players of this type need to be surrounded with good defenders to balance it out
Elusive Finisher/Slasher: Slashers are extremely effective at finishing at the basket with an array of layups. These are usually high flyers to specialise in dunking over defenders. However, due to this focus on inside scoring, the rest of a slasher's offensive game tends to be underdeveloped, meaning it is recommended they are surrounded with shooters to remain effective.
Floor General/Playmakers: Playmakers are the heart of the offence. They use their high basketball IQ to ensure everyone is in the right position at the right time on the offensive end. They use their unmatched passing ability to split defences open at will. Playmakers suffer from the fact that they are ball dominant and can turn the ball over at a high rate due to their usage rate.
Point Forward: A point forward is a taller playmaker. They use their size at the forward position to see 'over' defences, allowing them to see some passes that their smaller counterparts may not. However, they are not as quick as smaller playmakers, and this makes them less useful if the offence if they cannot shoot.
3PT Specialist: 3PT Specialists are offensive weapons. Their shooting ability makes them key to any championship contender in the current era of basketball. This ability means they must be guarded tightly when on the perimeter. However, pure shooters are less likely to have a well-rounded game and, as a result, are usually worse defenders and tend to be ineffective around the rim. If the shooter is on a cold streak, their value to a team drops drastically.
Stretch Big: A stretch big is a taller 3PT Specialist, using their height to rise and shoot over any defender. Their height makes them a unique piece to an offence, forcing the opposing bigmen to meet them at the perimeter, leaving the paint wide open. Due to their focus on three-point shooting, stretch bigs are generally worse at snagging rebounds as they reside closer to the perimeter.
Lockdown Defender: Lockdown defenders have the unique ability to affect a game with defence (defence wins championships?). They can force offensive players into cold streaks and gain easy baskets for their team. However, due to their heavy focus on the defensive end, lockdown defenders are less likely to have an offensive arsenal that strikes fear into other defences, and an elite defender can still be beaten by better offence.
Big Guard: Centers can also play like guards (e.g., Nikola Jokic)
Rim Protector: Rim Protectors are elite at preventing the ball from going in their hoop. Their defensive capabilities are valuable to any team. However, their offensive skill-set is lacking, making them a liability on offence and are ineffective against perimeter-oriented offences.
Rebounder: Rebounders will fight for every rebound on both ends of the floor; this can earn their team extra possessions and lead to quick fastbreaks. However, like other non-shooters, their skill-set is slowly going out of fashion.
Post Scorer: Post Scorers are your classic big-men - they love to get down low in the paint and can bang with just about anyone. In playoff games, when the game slows down or the shot clock is winding down, just dump the ball down low to them and let them get to work. However, basketball is becoming more perimeter-oriented and fast-paced, and as a result, post scoring is becoming a lost art.
Athletic Finisher: Athletic finishers are powerful, high flying, big-men who live around the rim. They can catch alley-oops from just about anywhere and posterise almost any other player they please. However, their offensive game is limited, and their skill-set is slowly going out of fashion in favour of shooting big-men.
